**Identifying blade structure**

request.raw_text: One of the long edges of the blade does not have a radius. Add radius to that long edge R=0,635cm

areas_to_change.action: Apply a constant-radius edge fillet of R=0.635 cm (6.35 mm).
areas_to_change.reference_geometry: The blade's currently unrounded longitudinal edge.
areas_to_change.location: Along the full exposed length of the sharp long edge, terminating at existing blade-end and hub-interface boundaries.
areas_to_change.description: Round the single long blade edge that presently lacks a radius so that it has a continuous 6.35 mm edge radius.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: All other blade edges and faces
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve their existing dimensions, radii, profiles, thickness, and surface geometry.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Blade end geometry and end holes
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Do not alter the rounded ends, angled end faces, holes, hole locations, or hole diameters.

areas_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Central square hub, supports, pins, and interfaces
areas_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve all hub geometry, clearances, connections, and relative component positions.
Maintain the existing blade lengths, orientations, crossing arrangement, and assembly alignment.

predicted_final_outcome.geometry: The previously sharp longitudinal blade edge will become a continuous convex fillet with a 0.635 cm radius; the remainder of the assembly will remain unchanged.
predicted_final_outcome.function: The added radius removes the unintended sharp edge and makes its treatment consistent with the intended rounded blade-edge design.
predicted_final_outcome.behavior: The blade should retain its existing fit, alignment, and motion while providing a smoother edge and reduced local stress concentration.
